amendments.reason: Delegate the code-surface fetch to the cases track's hardened fetcher: https only, no operator git configuration, hooks, submodules or filter drivers, GIT_* dropped, pin checked before checkout, and a checkout reused only when it holds exactly the pinned tree.
Update certifi from 2026.7.22 to 2026.10.19 for GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2, matching Nexus-ShadowScan#290; both distribution hashes checked against PyPI.

Add the --keys scheme: canonical-v1 compares reported and truth keys by tools.shadowbench.keys.canonical, refuses a scheme that merges truth keys of a case, and records a non-default scheme as key_scheme; the default exact scheme leaves every committed run re-scoring byte for byte.
State a non-default key scheme and the sandbox a run recorded (backend, namespaces or image and runtime, resource limits); reports of manifests without either are unchanged.

Run in fresh UTS and cgroup namespaces with a fixed host name, refuse to set it in the runner's UTS namespace, lower resource limits before anything runs (no core dumps, 4 GiB files, 4096 open files and processes), leave an already-up loopback alone, and add a contained mode for the OCI backend that refuses to skip its mounts on the runner's root file system.

Probe every stage namespace before running, pass resource limits and the host name to the stage, add the --sandbox oci backend (digest-pinned image, read-only root, only the run directory writable, four capabilities for the stage, no-new-privileges, seccomp, memory/CPU/pids limits, optional gVisor), and record isolation and the install_tools.sh resolved/ record (tool_install) in the manifest.

Install PyPI tools from committed universal hash locks with --require-hashes --no-deps and uv pip check, build the Fleet wrapper against a committed go.mod and go.sum instead of go mod tidy, take an optional tool list, and record the resolved set (freeze, go version -m, locks, SHA256SUMS) under TOOL_ROOT/resolved/.
The run_one stage doubles accept the optional sandbox argument _stage now takes.
The as-if-root runner.main helper also stubs the new namespace probe, as it already stubs unshare and the isolation checks.
The installer test asserts hash-locked installs (--require-hashes --no-deps, no go mod tidy) instead of the old version-pinned header.

Review fixes: a reported artifact path with a .. segment lies inside no truth directory, and a key reported more than once is labeled agent when any report is, so the agent tier does not depend on report order; no committed row has either shape, so every run of record re-scores byte for byte.
Review fix: the report calls the manifest's limits the requested ones, since each tool's manifest entry records the limits that held.

Review fixes: resource limits are set by prlimit in each tool invocation, soft and hard alike, not on the stage, whose result file and mock services were bound by them; the stage reports the limits that held, masks /etc/hostname and /etc/hosts with read-only files naming its host, and refuses limits no tool could run under.

Review fixes: record the limits each tool ran under, bind OCI tool trees at their configured paths, re-hash every binary install_tools.sh recorded and refuse to start on drift, empty out/resolved before copying the install record, and write rows with the tool root, scratch, output and harness paths replaced before their digest is taken.

Review fixes: create each venv afresh, build sdist-only distributions with the hash-locked setuptools of locks/build.txt and --no-build-isolation (uv does not enforce hashes on build constraints), and unset CDPATH so the locks path is a single line.
Review fix: skip the tool when its configured binary does not exist, as the PyPI adapters already did, so a subset install does not run absent binaries and score an error on every case.

Update virtualenv from 21.14.8 to 21.14.9 for GHSA-c978-59m8-c77v (CVE-2026-113722), which failed the strict pip-audit gate on main; dependency metadata is unchanged between the releases and both distribution hashes were checked against PyPI.

Review fixes: join a new, empty session keyring before anything from the case starts (a uid change keeps the session keyring, so tools could read the runner's keys), and cover /run and /tmp/.X11-unix, whose UNIX sockets (D-Bus, systemd-resolved, nscd, X) bridged the empty network namespace.

Review fixes: join a new session keyring before any version probe or stage starts, and strip group and other write from reclaimed regular files, as the estate runner does, so a 0666 report is no longer writable to the tools' uid.

Review fix: answer a malformed, negative or over-1 MiB Content-Length with 400 or 413 instead of raising, blocking a thread or allocating it, and drop socketserver's per-request tracebacks, which grew the root stage's stderr without bound.

Review fixes: umask 022; clear GOFLAGS, GOSUMDB, GONOSUMDB, GONOSUMCHECK, GOPRIVATE, GONOPROXY and GOINSECURE and ignore the go env file so the operator's settings cannot turn off -mod=readonly or the checksum database; reset and clean reused checkouts to exactly their pin; copy AI-Infra-Guard data afresh.

Review fixes: refuse a case listing a decoy, tolerated or expected key twice (a reported repeated decoy earned a true negative); require a row's seconds to be a finite, non-negative number; divide the McNemar tail by an integer (2.0**n overflowed from 1024 discordant cases); share the mixed-support check as mixed_support. Committed runs re-score byte for byte.

Review fixes: refuse a second run of a tool on one repository (the last row won, so an appended row could replace a failed scan) and require seconds to be a finite, non-negative number, raising RunsError. The committed 2026-10-09 metrics re-score byte for byte.
Review fix: report the scorer's RunsError as 'runs error:' with exit 2 instead of a traceback.

Regression tests for the review fixes: repeated decoy and tolerated keys are refused, bad row timings are refused, and the McNemar test holds past 1024 discordant cases and matches the previous formula below it.
Regression tests for the review fixes: a second run of a tool on one repository and bad run timings are refused.
Add the adapter rule that a file the tool wrote is read only through _report.read_text, since the tool controls its size and the adapter parses it as root.

Read the files the tool wrote through adapters/_report.read_text, which reads at most MAX_REPORT_BYTES (32 MiB) in 1 MiB chunks and raises ReportTooLarge (an OSError, already turned into an error result) instead of reading a tool-sized file whole as root; under the limit it returns what read_text did. Client configurations are parsed once per file identity (inode, size, mtime) however many reported servers send the lookup through them.

Read each invocation's stdout and stderr on threads and keep only their tails (STDOUT_KEEP, STDERR_KEEP characters) instead of communicate(), which held everything a tool printed in the root stage's memory; the deadline is unchanged: the tool must exit and its pipes close within its timeout.

Regression tests: _report.read_text matches read_text under its limit, raises over it and reserves no cap for a small report; oversized vet, AI-Infra-Guard, AgentDiscover and ShadowScan (including its code surface) reports are errors; AgentDiscover parses a configuration once per file identity.
